overview.heading: AK Recoil Buffer | Reduce Wear & Improve Cycling

blocks.text: Small upgrade. Big difference.

The AK recoil buffer is one of our most popular accessories for a reason. It’s an inexpensive upgrade that helps protect your rifle from unnecessary wear while improving overall cycling. Installation takes just minutes, but the benefits can last for thousands of rounds.
Whether you’re building a new AK or upgrading one you’ve owned for years, an AK recoil buffer is one of the easiest ways to add another layer of protection to your rifle.
Every time your rifle cycles, the bolt carrier impacts the rear of the receiver. Over time, that repeated metal-to-metal contact can contribute to unnecessary wear on critical components.

The AK recoil buffer installs between these contact points to help absorb impact before it reaches the receiver. By cushioning the bolt carrier, it helps reduce stress on internal parts while protecting your rifle during extended shooting sessions.
It’s a simple upgrade that can help extend the service life of your firearm.
Protection isn’t the only benefit.

When paired with any Texas Trigger Force Reset Trigger, the recoil buffer can also help improve cycling speed by reducing harsh rearward impact. The result is a smoother shooting experience that complements the fast mechanical reset of our trigger systems.
If you’re already running one of our AK FRTs, this is an upgrade worth adding.
There’s a reason this is one of our best-selling accessories.

Many customers add an AK recoil buffer to their order because it’s an affordable way to protect their investment while improving the overall shooting experience. It’s a small part that delivers noticeable value without adding complexity to your rifle.

overview.heading: A battle cry in axe form.

blocks.text: The Berserker Axe brings traditional Viking-inspired design together with materials made for real work. With its distinctive bearded blade, tough 1055 carbon steel, and genuine Tennessee hickory handle, this isn’t an axe that’s meant to spend its life hanging on the wall.

Take it camping. Keep it at the cabin. Use it to split firewood, process kindling, clear brush, or tackle everyday jobs around the property. At 19 inches long, the Berserker strikes a great balance between chopping power and portability.
The first thing you’ll notice about the Berserker Axe is its extended bearded blade.

Inspired by traditional Norse axe designs, the longer cutting edge provides plenty of surface area for chopping and splitting. The extended beard also gives you additional control when you need to choke up on the axe for more detailed work.
That versatility makes it useful for everything from breaking down firewood to making smaller, controlled cuts around camp.
And yes, it looks pretty mean doing it.
An axe needs steel that can take repeated impacts without becoming a constant maintenance project.

The Berserker uses 1055 carbon steel hardened to approximately 50–55 HRC . This steel is known for its toughness, impact resistance, and ability to maintain a working edge while remaining relatively easy to sharpen.

A manganese phosphate finish adds another layer of protection against corrosion and everyday wear. That’s especially useful when your axe spends time outdoors where rain, humidity, dirt, and changing temperatures come with the territory.
There’s a reason hickory has been used for quality axe handles for generations.

The Berserker Axe features a genuine Tennessee hickory handle that provides the strength needed for heavy swings while naturally helping absorb shock. The wood also offers a comfortable, traditional feel that’s difficult to duplicate with synthetic handles.
At 19 inches overall , there’s enough handle to generate real chopping power without making the axe cumbersome to carry.

overview.heading: Why Do Some Rifles Need a Transfer Bar?

blocks.text: Not all AK-pattern rifles are built to the same specifications. Manufacturing differences between brands can result in more than 2 mm of clearance between the bolt carrier group and the receiver wall.

When that happens, the standard transfer wire may not engage properly during cycling. Replacing it with the transfer bar corrects the spacing issue and allows the Diablo Trigger system to function reliably.
This isn’t an upgrade for added strength—it’s a compatibility solution designed for specific rifle platforms.
Like every Diablo Trigger component, the transfer bar is manufactured to meet strict durability standards and is thoroughly tested before it reaches customers.

Both the standard transfer wire and the transfer bar are engineered for long service life. The transfer bar simply provides the correct geometry for rifles that require it, helping eliminate fitment issues and simplifying installation.
Using the proper component from the start can save time during installation and help ensure dependable performance at the range.
Not every AK-pattern rifle requires a transfer bar . If you’re unsure whether your rifle needs one, review the Installation Guide before placing your order.
Installing the correct component from the beginning helps ensure a smoother installation and reliable operation of your Diablo Trigger system.

compatibility.heading: Transfer Bar | Diablo Trigger Compatibility Upgrade

blocks.text: The transfer bar is a required upgrade for certain AK-pattern rifles using the Diablo Trigger system. While many rifles operate perfectly with the standard transfer wire included in the kit, some models have additional clearance between the bolt carrier group (BCG) and the receiver wall. That extra spacing can prevent the standard wire from functioning correctly.
The transfer bar is designed to solve that issue, helping restore reliable operation and ensuring your Diablo Trigger performs as intended.
